Investors are chasing the crypto rally:

Call options volume in the largest Bitcoin ETF, $IBIT, surged to 1.58 million contracts on Wednesday, its largest daily volume on record.

$IBIT saw call options volume exceed 1 million contracts in each of the last 3 trading sessions from Wednesday through Friday.

As a result, call skew surged +0.05 points over the last 3 days, its biggest 3-day increase in at least 2 years.

Call skew measures the relative cost of upside versus downside options, so this sharp increase means investors are increasingly willing to pay up for upside exposure.

This is more than triple the average 3-day move since January 2025.

Crypto bulls are back in full force.

tweets.text:
When a company defaults now, lenders recover far less than they used to.

First-lien recovery fell to 61 cents on the dollar from 77, per S&P. Unsecured cratered from 29 to 9.

Two forces: distressed exchanges that reshuffle priority without cutting debt, and asset-light software borrowers with no collateral to seize.

Private credit is underwriting senior secured loans at record-tight spreads on recovery math that no longer holds. When defaults rise, losses land harder than any rating implies.

The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% in July, the most misleading number in the report.

Payrolls shrank 23,000, and prior months were revised down 103,000. The rate dropped only because people quit the labor force. Participation kept sliding and wage growth cooled to 3.2%.

🛢️This chart is a striking illustration of how the Strait of Hormuz crisis is reshaping—not just reducing—Middle East oil flows.

Fujairah and Sohar sit outside the Strait, and the surge in crude departures from these ports suggests they are increasingly functioning as bypass, transshipment and ship-to-ship transfer hubs for barrels that would historically have followed more direct routes through Hormuz.

The important point: this does not necessarily mean the UAE or Oman suddenly produced dramatically more crude.

It may also offer an indirect signal of growing “dark” vessel activity. As ships transit with limited or interrupted AIS visibility, tracking the full voyage becomes more difficult, and activity can effectively reappear outside Hormuz around hubs such as Fujairah and Sohar. The chart is not a direct measure of dark activity, but the changing pattern is consistent with a market in which voyage continuity has become harder to observe.

In other words, the disruption is showing up not only in oil prices and tanker rates, but in the geography—and visibility—of the physical oil market itself.

🚢Data from DSET

tweets.text: Morgan Stanley: "There was a concern voiced [Friday] that a transmission project in Texas (the 765 kV project),  which may not move forward, would invalidate all studies conducted regarding interconnecting proposed data centers to the ERCOT grid. This is an incorrect  interpretation, in our view. We actually view this development as a positive. Why? If  the 765 kV project does not move forward, several projects in the Base Load group  (those with potential interconnection dates in 2030-32) may be eliminated from this  group, which would be helpful because the 65 gigawatts in this group could fall to a  much smaller number, and this is positive because it means the Texas (ERCOT) grid  would be more likely to be able to accommodate interconnecting this smaller set of  projects. In our view, several of the PSP stocks we cover are favorable positioned  from this development: CIFR, HUT, GLXY, and MARA. We would also flag that  RIOT's sites are not subject to the ERCOT Batch process, and are therefore  increasingly valuable, in our view."

There are countless forks and shitcoins, but none have any appreciable value.

The market has convincingly proven that Bitcoin is in a league of it's own.

tweets.text:
With due respect to my ex-Bloomberg Intelligence colleague and all round solid guy, @mikemcglone11, who's copping a tonne of flak right now for being bearish on Bitcoin.

I loved my years working with Mike. Before I joined as the dedicated crypto analyst, he was already a Bitcoin stalwart, and one of the first people anywhere to flag stablecoins as the next big phenomenon, back in 2019. He was a lot more bullish back then too, funnily enough.

So I asked Mike onto @RealVision for a catch up and a proper look at his current thesis. He's said yes, we're just locking in the date.

Bloomberg's coverage has always been the establishment view, and on crypto that consensus skewed hard pro-Gensler, pro-Warren, apart from a few honest holdouts on the ETF desk. I loved the internal debates: taking on senior strategists and ESG zealots while calling the Bitcoin bottom in November and December 2022, and destroying the Bitcoin mining energy FUD with the actual data in 2023. Mike fought the anti-crypto sentiment inside the belly of the beast before anyone else. That deserves total respect. 

Markets need opposing views expressed freely, or they stop being markets. Long may that continue, on $btc and on Mike's thesis too.
